newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Eritrean in Mengistu attack trial alleges torture.
newsitem.headline: Eritrean in Mengistu attack trial alleges torture.

text.p: An Eritrean accused of attempting to assassinate exiled ex-Ethiopian leader Mengistu Haile Mariam said on Tuesday his genitals were permanently damaged by torture under Mengistu's rule.

Solomon Haile Ghebre Michael, 38, also alleged in the High Court that after his arrest last November, Zimbabwean security officers tortured him to force a confession to the attempted murder charges. He denies the allegations.

"The permanent damage that I have from torture under Mengistu is the genital damage I have and I am living with it," he said in Tigren through an interpretor. Solomon said he was held for six months in 1979 for opposing Mengistu.

He said Zimbabwean security officials had kicked him while he lay bleeding on the ground after they shot him last November following the alleged attempt to kill Mengistu as he strolled near his home in a posh Harare suburb.

"They (Zimbabwean officials) were telling me to admit what they wanted me to say and they were saying 'you came to kill Mengistu' and when I told them 'no, no,' they went on kicking and assaulting me," he said.
He said the officials drove him to Mengistu's house where they said they would call the former Ethiopian strongman to execute him on the spot unless he confessed.
Solomon's trial was delayed to allow a bullet wound to his arm to heal and to await the outcome of the trial of his alleged co-conspirator and countryman Abrahama Goietom Joseph Kinfe.

Abrahama was convicted last November on a plea of guilty to conspiring to murder Mengistu but later asked to change the plea on grounds he confessed under torture. The application was rejected and he is now appealing to the supreme court.

In court on Tuesday, Solomon denied he was sent to kill Mengistu by the Eritrean government. He come to Zimbabwe, he said, to establish contacts for his import and export venture and his government helped him get a visa because he was an ex-fighter of the Eritrean Liberation Army, one of the rebel groups that fought Mengistu.

Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993, two years after Mengistu fled rebels. Mengistu is being tried in absentia in Ethiopia on charges of genocide during his Dergue military group's 17-year rule.
